artifacts.body:
# PLAN — ISSUE-184: narrow toolchain mounts, component-wise home allowlist

Orientation: all logic lives in `internal/sandbox/toolchain.go`. Two helpers are wrong: `isSafeHomeToolchainPath` matches by raw string prefix, and `toolchainMountForBin` widens any `.../bin` on PATH to its parent. Fixing both makes `executorFlags` (Bubblewrap) and `codexPolicy` (native Codex) narrower automatically, because both get their mounts only through `HostToolchains` → `ToolchainMounts`.

**Shape**: Involved. The fix is small, but it is a security boundary with a layout allowlist to design, and the boundary test needs bwrap, which this sandbox does not have.

## What we know
- The PATH loop calls `toolchainMountForBin(dir)` for every admitted PATH entry (`internal/sandbox/toolchain.go:306-330`). That function returns the parent of any `bin`/`sbin` except `/`, `/usr`, `.local`, `.cargo` and `.bun` (`toolchain.go:379-388`). So `~/go/bin` → `~/go` and `/opt/x/bin` → `/opt/x`.
- `ToolchainMounts` drops a mount when an ancestor is also mounted (`toolchain.go:431-443`). So the `~/go` parent swallows the narrow `~/go/bin` mount that `addToolchainRoot` adds (`toolchain.go:160`).
- `isSafeHomeToolchainPath` uses `strings.HasPrefix(rel, prefix)` with entries such as `go/bin`, `.dotnet` and `.local/bin` (`toolchain.go:348-371`). That admits `go/binaries`, `.dotnet-x` and `.local/bin-x`.
- The two consumers have no toolchain logic of their own: `executor.go:78-83` (bwrap `--ro-bind`) and `native.go:87-95` (Codex `"<dir>"="read"`). `native.go:49` uses only `SandboxPath`.
- Explicit roots such as GOROOT, NVM_DIR, PYENV_ROOT, RUSTUP_HOME, /usr/local/go and the Homebrew prefixes are already mounted whole by `addToolchainRoot` (`toolchain.go:143-302`). This change does not affect them.
- Baseline: `go test ./internal/sandbox/` passes. `bwrap` and `codex` are not installed here (`command -v` found only `/usr/bin/go`).

## What we're assuming
- On Linux, Codex `:minimal` does not need `/usr/local` as a whole. Check: the env-gated `TestNativeCodexBoundary` on a host with Codex installed (PR review checklist).
- Intel-Mac Homebrew binaries in `/usr/local/bin` are symlinks into `/usr/local/Cellar`. To avoid a regression there, `/usr/local` stays a Homebrew prefix **only when goos is darwin**. Check: a table test with goos=darwin.

## Open questions
- Whether the real bwrap boundary passes (secret unreadable, `go version` runs). This cannot run in this sandbox (no bwrap). It will be answered by step 5's subtest under `SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1` on a bwrap host. Listed in the PR checklist.

## Dependents found (search: `toolchainMountForBin|isSafeHomeToolchainPath|HostToolchains|ToolchainMounts|SandboxPath|resolveHostToolchains`)
| Location | Depends on | Planned update |
|---|---|---|
| `toolchain.go:306-330` PATH loop | both helpers | Call the new layout-aware `toolchainMountForBin(dir, cleanHome, runtime.GOOS)` |
| `toolchain.go:342` `isSafeHomeToolchainPath` | — | Rewrite to compare whole components |
| `toolchain.go:379` `toolchainMountForBin` | — | Rewrite to use an explicit layout table |
| `executor.go:78-83` `executorFlags` | `HostToolchains`, `ToolchainMounts` | No change (narrows automatically) |
| `native.go:49`, `native.go:87-95` `codexPolicy` | `HostToolchains`, `ToolchainMounts`, `SandboxPath` | No change |
| `executor.go:150-200` `CheckToolExecutor` canary | executor mounts | No change. No fallback to a broader mount exists after this, so a toolchain that needs its parent fails the run or canary instead of widening |
| `build_cache.go` (#192) | none of these symbols. It only relies on `codexPolicy` skipping cache dirs (`native.go:94`) and on `IsBuildCacheKey` | No change |
| `build_cache_test.go` `TestCodexPolicyBuildCacheIsolation`, `TestExecutorFlagsBuildCacheIsolation`, `TestPrepareBuildCachesNeverCredentialHome` | real `HostToolchains` via `codexPolicy`/`executorFlags` | Unchanged; must stay green |
| `toolchain_test.go` `TestResolveHostToolchainsDiscoversMultiLanguageCachesWithoutCredentials` | both helpers | Unchanged. It still holds: `goBin` is mounted directly, `nvmNodeBin` is covered by `.nvm`, `.secret-keys/bin` is rejected |
| `toolchain_test.go` `TestNativeAndBubblewrapOfflineLanguageBuildAndTest` | real mounts (env-gated) | Unchanged |
| `executor_test.go:87` `TestToolExecutorBoundary` | real bwrap mounts | Append one subtest (step 5). Existing assertions untouched |
| `native_test.go:203` `TestNativeCodexBoundary` | real Codex policy | Unchanged |
| Docs (`README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `docs/*.md`) | grep shows no description of toolchain mounting | No change |

## Design
**Component matching.** `isSafeHomeToolchainPath` splits `rel` on `/` and splits each allowlist entry the same way, with the trailing `/` dropped. A path matches when the entry's components are a prefix of rel's components. Today's semantics are preserved: an entry and its descendants match. A shared sibling string such as `binaries` does not.

**Layout table.** `knownInstallLayouts` holds patterns; `*` matches exactly one component. Each pattern ends in `bin`/`sbin`, and the mount is the pattern minus its last component.
- Home-relative (matched against the canonical HOME, and also passing `isSafeHomeToolchainPath`):
  - `.nvm/versions/node/*/bin`
  - `.pyenv/versions/*/bin`
  - `.rustup/toolchains/*/bin`
  - `.asdf/installs/*/*/bin`
  - `.local/share/mise/installs/*/*/bin`
  - `.local/share/fnm/node-versions/*/installation/bin`
  - `.fnm/node-versions/*/installation/bin`
  - `.volta/tools/image/*/*/bin`
  - `.sdkman/candidates/*/*/bin`
- Absolute:
  - `/usr/local/go/bin`
  - `/opt/homebrew/{bin,sbin}`
  - `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/{bin,sbin}`
  - darwin only: `/usr/local/{bin,sbin}`

Anything else returns `binDir` itself. That includes `~/go/bin`, `/opt/<x>/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, and Linux `/usr/local/bin`.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- Keep generic expansion with a denylist (e.g. skip `go`): fails open for every unknown layout.
- Detect GOROOT by marker files (`VERSION`, `src/runtime`): heuristic, and it lets a crafted directory widen mounts. GOROOT is already covered by the `GOROOT` env and `/usr/local/go`.

## Steps
1. `toolchain.go`: add a `hasPathComponents(rel, prefix string) bool` helper and use it in `isSafeHomeToolchainPath`. The allowlist stays unchanged.
2. `toolchain.go`: add the `knownInstallLayouts` table and change the signature to `toolchainMountForBin(binDir, cleanHome, goos string) string`. Update its doc comment.
3. `toolchain.go` PATH loop: compute `cleanHome` once before the loop and pass it with `runtime.GOOS`.
4. `toolchain_test.go`: add table tests only (existing test untouched):
   - `TestIsSafeHomeToolchainPathComponents`
   - `TestToolchainMountForBinKnownLayouts`: every layout, darwin vs linux `/usr/local/bin`, and the rejected cases
   - `TestToolchainMountsExcludeGoSrc`: synthetic HOME, built through `codexPolicy` and `executorFlags`
5. `executor_test.go` `TestToolExecutorBoundary`: append a `t.Run("toolchain mounts exclude go/src", ...)` subtest. It sets a synthetic HOME with `go/bin` and `go/src/private/secret.txt`, sets PATH to `<home>/go/bin` plus the real `go`'s directory, and sets GOROOT from `go env GOROOT`. It asserts that `e.Run` shows `cat` of the secret fails and `go version` succeeds. It skips when `exec.LookPath("bwrap")` fails, inside the existing `SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR` gate.
6. Add `changes/unreleased/184-narrow-toolchain-mounts.md`: one bullet in the style of `192-build-caches.md`.
7. Run `gofmt -s -l`, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, `go test ./...` and `make check`.

## Follow-ups (not in scope)
- The Go SDK from `golang.org/dl` (`~/sdk/go<v>`) is not allowlisted under HOME. Consider a WorkUnit if users report it.
- A canary assertion that probes a sibling of each mounted toolchain bin is a hardening idea for a separate WorkUnit.

## Operator guidance

> Planner: keep the plan compact. Before planning, search for existing tests, docs and call sites that depend on toolchain discovery, toolchainMountForBin and isSafeHomeToolchainPath (including #192's build_cache.go and toolchain_test.go), and list each with its planned update.
